# Releases

Releases are managed by [Release Please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please), not by the archived deployment workflow.

## Release flow

1. Merge changes into `main` using merge commits. Keep individual pull-request commits Conventional Commit-compliant (`feat:`, `fix:`, `perf:`, and so on); Release Please reads the commit history on `main` since the previous release.
2. The `Release Please` workflow opens or updates a release pull request when the commit history requires a release.
3. Review the generated version and changelog. Merge the release pull request.
4. Release Please updates `version.txt` and `CHANGELOG.md`, creates the version tag, and publishes the GitHub Release.

`version.txt` is the single application-version source. `CHANGELOG.md` is generated by Release Please. Do not bump the version, edit the generated changelog, or create release tags manually during the normal release process.

Conventional Commit types that describe user-visible changes determine the release increment. A `feat` normally requests a minor release; a `fix` or `perf` requests a patch release. Breaking changes must use the Conventional Commits breaking-change marker or footer.

## Workflow configuration

The workflow uses `secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN`. The secret must contain a token authorized to write repository contents, issues, and pull requests. GitHub Actions must also be allowed to create pull requests in the repository's Actions settings.

The release workflow runs on pushes to `main`. It does not build or publish distro packages.

## Packaging and archived deployment

GitHub Releases currently provide source archives. Automated deployment to AUR or nixpkgs is not configured.

The previous deployment workflow remains disabled at [`docs/archive/deploy.yml.disabled`](../docs/archive/deploy.yml.disabled). It coupled GitHub releases with AUR publishing and exposed SSH credentials to an external package build. Do not re-enable it without a separate security and functionality review.
